question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+4}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(1+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{0}{1+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$
